Resolves #18978

Related: #9486 · #18762

🪢 *Unlock a grid's only locked-end column and the column is gone: no header, no cells, no error — while its instance lives on. The region's toolbar was torn down with the moving column's button still inside it.*

## What changes

`header.Wrapper#updateHeaders` handled each region in one pass: create or refresh its toolbar, or destroy it when the region holds no column. `grid.Container#onColumnsMutate` re-homes the header buttons only AFTER that call, so a region that emptied at runtime lost the button of the column that had just left it.

The pass is now three steps: create or refresh the toolbars of the regions that hold columns, re-home the buttons (`applyColumnButtonOrder`) when a region emptied, destroy the emptied toolbar. The button is moved, never rebuilt. The start region had the same teardown and is covered the same way.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, CI-executed e2e tier) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-4). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: restoration (`fix`).

| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same two arms — locking again gives three bodies, the button, and every cell back in the locked region. |

## Deltas from ticket

- The arms drive the fixture through one parametrized driver action, `setLocked` (`field`, `locked`), instead of two fixed ones.
- On `dev` the unlock also threw `util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-grid-body-6` on the pooled fixture. It is gone with this fix (30 of 30 arms run with the page-error gate on); I did not trace it separately.

## Test Evidence

Red-first on `dev@4802862b73`: 2 of 2 red — `buttonIds: []` after the unlock, for the end and for the start region. The fix is an ordering, so the red-first run is its mutation. `--repeat-each=15`: 30 of 30.
